messages:
Alex Kim: Heads-up — draft release notes are ready for review. Need a short internal blurb for the staff email and a canary rollback criteria.
Priya Shah: On it. Can we keep the internal blurb to one paragraph + 2 bullets for user impact?
Ben Torres: +1. Also confirm which model version we’re pinning for Hosted (is it rwd-3b-v2 or the quantized variant?)
Alex Kim: We’re pinning rwd-3b-v2 for the first 48h, fallback to rwd-3b-qv1 if latency spikes. Will add that to the notes.
deploy-bot: deploy started: staging -> canary at 17:12 UTC (build 2026.03.21-57).
Morgan Lee: Quick ask — include the metrics team in the blurb so they can watch prompt regression.
Priya Shah: Draft blurb: "Today we’re rolling out model performance and stability fixes. Users should see faster response times at high concurrency. If you own downstream prompt logic, please review your evals for regressions." Thoughts?
Isabel Ramos: Love that. Add: "Canary window: 90m. Rollback if 95p latency > 800ms or user-error rate increases > 0.5% vs baseline."
Ben Torres: Sounds good. For rollback automation: ops will manually cut to rwd-3b-qv1; if deploy-bot sees error spike it will notify @eng-oncall and tag the release thread.
deploy-bot: canary health: all checks passing (latency, logs, infra).
Alex Kim: Finalize: Priya will post internal note at +30m, Morgan will own metric watch, Ben owns rollback ops, Isabel will update the release notes doc with the exact rollback steps.
Priya Shah: Copy. I’ll post the internal blurb and link to the detailed RN doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/rn/2026-03-21-model-stability.
Morgan Lee: I’ll add the eval dashboard to the RN doc and set alert thresholds.
Isabel Ramos: Putting the explicit rollback command in the doc now: `deploybot rollback --release rwd-3b-v2 --target rwd-3b-qv1 --reason "canary regression"`.
Alex Kim: Great work. If anything changes during the canary, shout here and we’ll pause the blast. :loudspeaker: :thumbsup:
